editorial:
You follow Peter, a brave kid from a London orphanage, as he gets pulled into Neverland and meets Hook, Tiger Lily, and the scary Blackbeard. The world is bright, loud, and full of flying ships, so it feels like a big adventure from the start. You can tell the movie wants to be a fun origin story, and the cast keeps things moving even when the story gets messy. It is not perfect, but it has enough energy to keep younger viewers interested.

The action scenes are colorful and easy to follow, and some moments are genuinely exciting for kids. On the downside, the plot jumps around and the humor does not always land, so adults may feel less invested. Still, if you want a loud family movie night, this can work. The costumes and sets look great, and the final battle gives you a clear payoff. Stream it in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video, rent it on Apple TV, or grab the 4K Blu-ray if you like collecting.
endingExplained: In the final battle, Peter finally learns to fly and uses that power to stop Blackbeard. Blackbeard falls into the dangerous Neverland below, and Peter helps save Tiger Lily and the others. Afterward, Peter returns to the orphanage and frees the other children, bringing them to Neverland. Hook is still his friend for now, but the ending hints that their friendship will not last forever. You see Peter fully become Pan, ready for more adventures.
targetAudience: Ideal for families with kids who enjoy fantasy adventures.
